title: Kennibec potato (Kennebec): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Kennibec potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Kennibec potato is a potato variety. 90 to 100 days to harvest, 21.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Kennibec is a registered potato variety, also sold or known as Kennebec or Kennebec potato. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1994 as NSIC 1994 Po 03. It comes from registered by BPI BNCRDC (introduced variety). It takes 90 to 100 days from planting to harvest, with 21.17 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Kennebec or Kennebec potato, this is the same potato. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [potato variety finder](/crop-varieties/potato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items: **Days to harvest:** 90 to 100 days from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 21.17 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Kennibec potato takes 90 to 100 days from planting to harvest. That is 8.5 days faster than the average of the 11 potato varieties with a day count, 103.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 21.17 t/ha matches the average of its group, 21.79. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 90 to 100 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit potato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have whitish flesh and yellowish/ smooth skin. Dry matter is 18.9 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Whitish flesh, smooth yellowish skin, elliptic to oblong tubers, dry matter about 19 percent.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of seven varieties URC farmers in Benguet are testing against Granola in 2026. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Kennibec potato

It suits highland areas. Potato grows in the cool highlands of Benguet, Mountain Province and Bukidnon. Plant clean seed tubers, and pick a variety rated against late blight for the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Kennebec the same as Kennibec?
items.a: Yes. Kennebec is another name for Kennibec, registered as NSIC 1994 Po 03. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 90 to 100 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 21.17 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Kennibec?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
